Why Pushes Get Rejected" says "Rebased commits get **new SHAs**, so your copy diverges" and "A normal push is rejected as non-fast-forward".

findings.summary: The Merge Flavors section says rebase then fast-forward gives a linear history, but its code block ends with `git merge --no-ff`, which produces a merge commit.
findings.evidence: Bullet: "Rebase first, then fast-forward for a **linear** history". Code: "git rebase main", "git switch main", "git merge --no-ff feature", with the note "no-ff keeps the branch visible".
findings.fix: Show `git merge feature` (a fast-forward) as the linear example. If `--no-ff` stays, label it as the alternative that keeps a merge commit.

findings.summary: The `--onto` recovery note is ambiguous about whose old tip `old-sha` is.
findings.evidence: "teammate fix: old-sha = your old tip" next to "Share the **old SHA** so they can run `--onto`"
findings.fix: Write: "old-sha = the branch tip before the rewrite (the rewriter shares it); the teammate runs `git rebase --onto origin/feat <old-sha>`."

findings.summary: The reflog undo example uses `HEAD@{5}`, but the sample output shows no such entry and nothing explains how to choose n.
findings.evidence: The sample reflog shows only "HEAD@{0}: rebase (finish)" and "HEAD@{3}: commit: add login". The undo block then runs "git reset --hard HEAD@{5}". The steps say "find the line before the rebase" without showing it.
findings.fix: Extend the sample reflog to show the pre-rebase entry, for example `HEAD@{5}: rebase (start)` with the commit just before it. Use that same n in the reset command.

findings.summary: The reflog is presented as a full recovery path after `--abort`, but the conflict resolution in progress at the time of the abort is never committed.
findings.evidence: "Aborting after resolving: the finished work is gone" with "`git reflog`, then `git reset --hard HEAD@{n}` brings it back."
findings.fix: Say that the reflog recovers only commits already replayed. Uncommitted conflict resolutions are lost after `--abort`, so use `git rerere` or commit a backup branch first.

findings.summary: The tip says `git diff backup-feature` confirms nothing changed, but this only holds when the rebase didn't move onto a newer base.
findings.evidence: "Compare `git diff backup-feature` to confirm nothing changed."
findings.fix: Say: "If the base didn't change, `git diff backup-feature` should be empty. Otherwise use `git range-diff backup-feature...`." Alternatively, replace the tip with `git range-diff` guidance.

findings.summary: The `git range-diff` example uses undefined `old` and `new` placeholders in a form that differs from how the command was introduced.
findings.evidence: Code: "git range-diff main old new". The syllabus form is `git range-diff old..new`, and nothing here says what `old` and `new` are.
findings.fix: Use concrete refs, for example `git range-diff main backup-feature feature`. Add a note: "old = backup or ORIG_HEAD, new = rebased branch".
